verdict.rationale: Vapi's docs describe a Voice Library in the dashboard where developers can browse and preview text-to-speech voices from any Vapi-supported provider and copy a voice ID onto an assistant. They also document using custom voices with any supported provider through the assistant's `voice` property. This shows a voice catalog and multi-provider support, but the pack never names the TTS providers or shows how large the library is, so 'broad' and 'multiple providers' are only implied. Missing for 10: an enumerated list of supported TTS providers, evidence of the library's size or breadth, and independent or hands-on corroboration of voice and provider choice.

support.subject: As a developer, I can choose from a broad voice library or plug in multiple TTS providers to get the voice I want

citations.quote: The **Voice Library** in the [Vapi Dashboard] lists every voice available to your organization. Browse and preview voices there, then copy a voice's ID to use on an assistant.
Find, preview, and use text-to-speech voices from any Vapi-supported provider
You can use your own custom voice with any supported provider by setting the `voice` property in your assistant configuration
